appendices.methodology:
This assessment evaluates compliance against the following framework(s): India DPDPA, ISO 27001, across 120 in-scope requirements.

Basis of Assessment:
Each in-scope requirement receives one conclusion. The analysis engine reviews the submitted documents and questionnaire responses and proposes an outcome with cited evidence. A consultant reviews the evidence and individually approves, edits or rejects every proposal. Only individually approved conclusions appear in this report; no outcome, score or finding is produced by the AI on its own.

Outcome Definitions:
- Compliant: the requirement is met and supported by evidence
- Partially Compliant: the requirement is met in part
- Non-Compliant: the requirement is not met
- Insufficient Evidence: the evidence provided does not support a conclusion either way
- Not Applicable: the requirement does not apply within the assessed scope

Scoring Basis:
Scores are computed only from conclusions a consultant has individually approved. Each approved outcome counts as follows: Compliant 100 points, Partially Compliant 50 points, Non-Compliant 0 points. Not Applicable and Insufficient Evidence are excluded from the scoring denominator. Insufficient Evidence is not treated as Non-Compliant; the number of requirements with insufficient evidence is reported next to each framework score. Requirements excluded at scoping are not scored. A framework is scored only when every in-scope requirement has an approved conclusion. Section scores are the average of their requirement points; domain and framework scores are weighted averages using the published weights below.

Framework Structure and Weights:
- India DPDPA (2023): 41 requirements in 6 domains. Domain weights: Obligations of Data Fiduciary 30%, Rights of Data Principal 20%, Special Provisions 20%, Consent Management (Detailed) 10%, Cross-Border Data Transfer 10%, Breach Notification 10%.
- ISO 27001 (2022): 93 requirements in 4 domains. Domain weights: Organizational Controls 35%, People Controls 15%, Physical Controls 15%, Technological Controls 35%.
Requirements are referenced by clause or control identifier for each selected framework; requirement descriptions are summarised for assessment purposes and do not reproduce the source standard. Scores are computed and reported independently for each framework; no score is combined across frameworks.

Rating Thresholds:
- 80-100%: Compliant
- 60-79%: Partially Compliant
- 40-59%: Needs Significant Improvement
- 0-39%: Non-Compliant

Risk Classification:
Each gap carries the risk level (Critical, High, Medium, Low) approved by the consultant, reflecting regulatory exposure, potential penalties under INDIA DPDPA and impact on affected individuals (for INDIA DPDPA), and likely impact on the confidentiality, integrity and availability of information (for ISO 27001). Remediation priority on each gap is derived from its approved risk level.

Disclaimer:
This assessment provides guidance based on the information and evidence provided and is not legal advice. Consult qualified legal counsel for definitive compliance determinations under INDIA DPDPA. For ISO 27001, it is not a certification audit; certification decisions rest with an accredited certification body or qualified assessor.

summary.basis_of_assessment: This document constitutes an evidence-based compliance gap assessment. It is not a formal compliance audit and does not constitute legal advice. Findings are based on documents submitted for review and information disclosed by the organization's representatives, and every conclusion was individually approved by a consultant. These conclusions reflect the evidence considered up to the evidence cut-off stated above.
summary.confidentiality: This report is prepared solely for the use of the named organization. It should not be shared with third parties without the organization's explicit consent. Golden Advisory and the named organization are the intended recipients of this report.

narrative.text: Consent, breach notification and processor contracts are the weakest areas; rights handling and notices are largely in place.
Policies and organisational controls are mostly implemented; access reviews and vulnerability management are the material gaps.

limitations: This assessment does not include technical penetration testing, source code review, network security assessment, or any form of independent technical verification. Where the selected framework(s) include physical or environmental controls, findings on those controls are based on disclosed information and submitted documents, not on physical inspection or testing.

All findings reflect the information provided to the assessor at the time of the assessment. The assessor has not independently verified the accuracy or completeness of information provided. Material omissions or inaccuracies in disclosed information would affect the reliability of findings.

For requirements rated as Non-Compliant or Partially Compliant at a Critical or High risk level, independent verification by qualified legal counsel or a certified privacy professional (for INDIA DPDPA requirements), or by a qualified information security auditor (for ISO 27001), is strongly recommended before relying on those findings for regulatory submissions, board reporting, or contractual representations.

Most DPDPA 2023 obligations on Data Fiduciaries, and its penalty provisions, commence in mid-May 2027 (DPDP Rules 2025, G.S.R. 846(E)); findings against those obligations are a readiness assessment, not a determination of current non-compliance. Until then, obligations under the Information Technology Act, 2000, s.43A and the SPDI Rules, 2011 continue to apply and were not assessed.
scope: ISO 27001: 79 requirements in scope (Physical Controls excluded: single cloud-hosted office)

executive.text: The organisation has a sound policy base, but several controls that protect customer data exist on paper only and are not operated.
The most serious exposures are consent that is unlikely to be valid, no procedure for notifying the regulator of a breach, and access rights that are never reviewed.
Most gaps are process gaps with clear owners, and closing access control and supplier security once addresses findings under both frameworks.

cross_framework.text: Weak access governance appears under both DPDPA security safeguards and ISO 27001 access-rights controls.

top_risks.title: Consent is collected through pre-ticked boxes
top_risks.description: The sign-up journey and the marketing preference centre both pre-select consent. No record links a consent to the notice the user saw.
top_risks.business_impact: Consent obtained this way is unlikely to be valid, so processing that depends on it would lack a lawful basis once DPDPA obligations commence; this affects the full 2.1 million-customer marketing base.
top_risks.requirement_title: Lawful basis for processing with free, specific, informed consent
top_risks.action_title: Replace pre-ticked consent with an affirmative opt-in and log the notice version shown

top_risks.title: No procedure to notify the Data Protection Board of a breach
top_risks.description: The incident response plan covers containment only. It names no owner, timeline or template for notifying the Board or affected individuals.
top_risks.business_impact: A breach handled under the current plan would miss the statutory notification, which carries the highest penalty tier under the Act.
top_risks.requirement_title: Breach notification to Data Protection Board
top_risks.action_title: Adopt a breach-notification runbook with owner, 72-hour timeline and regulator templates

top_risks.title: Access rights are never reviewed
top_risks.description: No periodic review of user access is evidenced for production systems. 14 leaver accounts were still active at the cut-off.
top_risks.business_impact: Former staff and over-privileged users can reach customer data, the most common root cause of insider and credential-based breaches.
top_risks.action_title: Run quarterly access reviews for production and customer-data systems

top_risks.title: No defined cadence for patching technical vulnerabilities
top_risks.description: Scans run ad hoc; 23 critical CVEs older than 90 days were open on internet-facing hosts at the cut-off.
top_risks.business_impact: Known, exploitable weaknesses on public systems are the leading entry point for ransomware.
top_risks.action_title: Set patch SLAs (critical 15 days) and report monthly to the risk committee

top_risks.title: Customer database access is not restricted by role
top_risks.description: Encryption at rest is in place, but 41 engineers hold read access to the customer database with no role-based restriction.
top_risks.business_impact: Broad access raises the likelihood and scale of a personal-data breach and weakens the 'reasonable security safeguards' defence.
top_risks.action_title: Introduce role-based access to the customer database

top_risks.title: Data Processor contracts lack data-protection clauses
top_risks.description: Seven of nine processor contracts reviewed contain no security, breach-notice or deletion obligations.
top_risks.business_impact: The company remains liable for its processors' failures with no contractual recourse or audit right.
top_risks.action_title: Issue a data-processing addendum to all processors

top_risks.title: Supplier security is not assessed before onboarding
top_risks.description: A supplier questionnaire exists but is not used; no supplier risk tiering is recorded.
top_risks.business_impact: Third-party compromise cannot be anticipated or contracted against.
top_risks.action_title: Tier suppliers by data access and assess tier-1 suppliers annually

top_risks.title: Customer data is retained indefinitely
top_risks.description: The retention policy sets periods for HR records only; customer and KYC data have no retention period or deletion job.
top_risks.business_impact: Holding data beyond its purpose enlarges breach impact and conflicts with the storage-limitation duty.
top_risks.requirement_title: Data retention limited to purpose fulfilment
top_risks.action_title: Define retention periods for customer and KYC data and automate deletion

top_risks.title: Business continuity plan has never been tested
top_risks.description: The BCP is approved but no test or exercise has been recorded since it was written in 2024.
top_risks.business_impact: Recovery times for core platforms are unknown; an outage could exceed customer contractual commitments.
top_risks.action_title: Test the BCP for the payments platform and record results

top_risks.title: Grievance channel has no response timeline
top_risks.description: Grievances are received through a shared mailbox with no tracking or response-time commitment.
top_risks.business_impact: Unresolved complaints can be escalated to the Data Protection Board.
top_risks.action_title: Publish a grievance form with tracking and a 30-day response commitment

consultant: Approve funding for a consent-management platform before the May 2027 DPDPA commencement.
Confirm the CISO as accountable owner for vulnerability management and set the patch SLA as a board-tracked KPI.

observations.title: Consent is collected through pre-ticked boxes
observations.observation: The sign-up journey and the marketing preference centre both pre-select consent. No record links a consent to the notice the user saw.
observations.risk: Consent obtained this way is unlikely to be valid, so processing that depends on it would lack a lawful basis once DPDPA obligations commence; this affects the full 2.1 million-customer marketing base.
observations.recommendation: Replace pre-selected consent with an unticked, purpose-specific opt-in on every channel. Log each consent with the notice version shown, timestamp and channel, and re-collect consent for the existing marketing base before relying on it.

observations.title: No procedure to notify the Data Protection Board of a breach
observations.observation: The incident response plan covers containment only. It names no owner, timeline or template for notifying the Board or affected individuals.
observations.risk: A breach handled under the current plan would miss the statutory notification, which carries the highest penalty tier under the Act.
observations.recommendation: Extend the incident response plan with a notification runbook: named decision owner, 72-hour clock, Board and data-principal templates, and an evidence log. Test it in a tabletop exercise each year.

observations.title: Access rights are never reviewed
observations.observation: No periodic review of user access is evidenced for production systems. 14 leaver accounts were still active at the cut-off.
observations.risk: Former staff and over-privileged users can reach customer data, the most common root cause of insider and credential-based breaches.
observations.recommendation: Run quarterly access recertification for production and customer-data systems with manager sign-off. Disable leaver accounts within 24 hours through an HR-triggered workflow and keep review evidence.

observations.title: No defined cadence for patching technical vulnerabilities
observations.observation: Scans run ad hoc; 23 critical CVEs older than 90 days were open on internet-facing hosts at the cut-off.
observations.risk: Known, exploitable weaknesses on public systems are the leading entry point for ransomware.
observations.recommendation: Adopt patch SLAs by severity (critical 15 days, high 30 days), scan internet-facing assets weekly, and report open critical vulnerabilities to the risk committee monthly.

observations.title: Customer database access is not restricted by role
observations.observation: Encryption at rest is in place, but 41 engineers hold read access to the customer database with no role-based restriction.
observations.risk: Broad access raises the likelihood and scale of a personal-data breach and weakens the 'reasonable security safeguards' defence.
observations.recommendation: Define role-based access profiles for the customer database, remove standing engineer access, and route exceptions through time-bound, approved break-glass access with session logging.

observations.title: Data Processor contracts lack data-protection clauses
observations.observation: Seven of nine processor contracts reviewed contain no security, breach-notice or deletion obligations.
observations.risk: The company remains liable for its processors' failures with no contractual recourse or audit right.
observations.recommendation: Issue a data-processing addendum covering security, breach notice within 24 hours, sub-processing, audit rights and deletion at exit, and track signature to completion.

observations.title: Supplier security is not assessed before onboarding
observations.observation: A supplier questionnaire exists but is not used; no supplier risk tiering is recorded.
observations.risk: Third-party compromise cannot be anticipated or contracted against.
observations.recommendation: Tier suppliers by data access, assess tier-1 suppliers before onboarding and annually, and record the risk decision in the supplier register.

observations.title: Customer data is retained indefinitely
observations.observation: The retention policy sets periods for HR records only; customer and KYC data have no retention period or deletion job.
observations.risk: Holding data beyond its purpose enlarges breach impact and conflicts with the storage-limitation duty.
observations.recommendation: Set retention periods for customer and KYC data by purpose and legal basis, and automate deletion or anonymisation at expiry with a monthly exception report.

observations.title: Business continuity plan has never been tested
observations.observation: The BCP is approved but no test or exercise has been recorded since it was written in 2024.
observations.risk: Recovery times for core platforms are unknown; an outage could exceed customer contractual commitments.
observations.recommendation: Test the BCP for the payments platform against target recovery times, record the results and fix gaps found before the next test cycle.

observations.title: Grievance channel has no response timeline
observations.observation: Grievances are received through a shared mailbox with no tracking or response-time commitment.
observations.risk: Unresolved complaints can be escalated to the Data Protection Board.
observations.recommendation: Publish a grievance form with ticket tracking and a 30-day response commitment, and report volumes and ageing to the DPO monthly.
